theme: Water · Queensland: cloudy during the event, radar with river gauges
title: Laidley, Queensland: after the October 2026 floods
place: Lockyer Valley, South East Queensland, Australia
product: NISAR L2 GCOV, L-band, Frequency A, HHHH and HVHV
what_happened: Severe weather and flooding affected southern Queensland from 21 to 28 October 2026. Lockyer Valley, which includes Laidley, was among the local government areas activated for disaster assistance.

sources.label: Queensland Reconstruction Authority activation summary, 21-28 October 2026

mechanism: Wetter ground and plants can alter L-band scattering. A shared offset may also include processing-version effects. The relative view subtracts one median per period and polarisation; spatially varying effects and real widespread change can remain or be suppressed. Blue or red is not a physical classification.

evidence.label: Laidley Creek at Warrego Highway (143229A)
evidence.note: Hourly mean gauge height. Quality code 130 (not coded), so not validated by the data owner. Gauge height is not a flood depth on the land.
evidence.credit: Queensland Government, Water Monitoring Information Portal, CC BY 4.0

independent_evidence.text: A river gauge and a government disaster activation confirm the event. They do not confirm water at any pixel.

reference_extent.text: No official inundation boundary for this event was found to compare against.

limits: The before and after images come from different processing versions (P05023 and P05036). A same-acquisition test on another track found the newer version about 0.34 dB darker in HH and 0.25 dB darker in HV. The maps here are not adjusted for this.
The after image was taken at 17:57 AEST on 25 October. The gauge chart shows what the creek was doing at that moment.
Across the wider study area, larger 13-day rainfall totals went with smaller brightening (Spearman -0.43 for HH), so rainfall totals alone do not explain the pattern.
Copernicus Sentinel-2 tiles acquired on 25 October were 96 to 100 percent cloud covered (whole-tile metadata).
use_for: Deciding where to send assessment crews or request aerial imagery first when cloud blocks optical satellites.
Keeping a dated, reproducible record of where the surface changed more than it normally does.
not_for: It is not a inundation boundary map.
It is not a alert or road-closure product. NISAR revisits every 12 days.
It has not been validated against a surveyed flood boundary.
series_note: Ten dates from 27 June to 25 October 2026. No product was returned for 2 August, so one step is 24 days. Only the last date uses the newer processing version (P05036).
radar_summary: After heavy rain, the whole analysis window brightened by +3.27 dB in HH. Farmland and grassland brightened by +3.40 dB, versus +1.95 dB on the hard-surface reference. The whole-window change over the preceding 12 days was -0.16 dB. This is consistent with wetter ground and plants. The after image is the only key date made with P05036 rather than P05023, so environmental change and processing-version effects cannot be fully separated. Switch the change map to Relative to the whole window to find places that changed more or less than their surroundings.
agreement: River gauges and rainfall establish wet-weather context, not the cause of every radar change. Window-median subtraction changes the display reference only; it neither separates the two causes nor validates an inundation boundary.
optical_text: On 25 October 2026, catalogued Sentinel-2 tiles had 95.98–99.83% cloud cover (whole-tile metadata, not local pixel QA). No optical comparison labels were produced for these Queensland views; other dates are not established as unusable. Radar can observe through cloud, but that alone does not validate a change interpretation. River gauges and rainfall records provide independent context instead.
tour: Compare the dated radar observations and consult the river and rainfall context.
The raw change image is broadly red because much of the landscape brightened after heavy rain; a processing-version difference is also present.
Choose Relative to the whole window: it shows where change is above or below the whole-window median, not a corrected physical measurement.
Read the dated gauge and rainfall evidence, alongside the processing-version limitation.
Explore either polarisation and switch back to Raw change. Click readings remain raw changes.
headline: After heavy rain the whole window brightened by a median 3.3 dB in HH, against -0.7 to +0.4 dB in every earlier 12-day interval.
map_note: No optical reference for this event: Sentinel-2 scenes on 25 October were about 96 to 99.8% cloud-covered (whole-tile metadata). This is the situation radar is for; here the independent evidence is river gauges and rainfall.
